subject: TEST-NUMVAL function
notes:
Citation re-derived mechanically: cite.py --check 15.93.3 "Argument-1 shall be an alphanumeric or national literal or a data item of class alphanumeric or national." -> OK (§15.93.3 rule 1). READ: IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified line 686 carries ["TEST-NUMVAL"] = Uniform('s', "§15.93.3 r1"); Admissible('s') = [Alphanumeric, NumericEditedDeEditing, National]; Violation() intersects that set with CandidateClasses(op) and IntrinsicBinder.BindIntrinsicCore calls CheckArgumentClasses(sig, args) AFTER the arity check and BEFORE every per-function arm, so the row is live for this function. Both halves of the one sentence checked. (a) A numeric literal/item, a boolean item, an index item, an object reference and a pointer are all rejected (class Numeric/Boolean/Index/Object/Pointer are absent from the 's' set); the registered negative pb58-testnumval-num compiles COMPUTE T = FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL(N9) over PIC 9(3) and is reject-at 2002 2014 2023 (manifest.json:194). (b) The admitted classes are exactly right, INCLUDING the one that looks like over-acceptance and is not: the model folds PIC A into PicCategory.Alphanumeric (PicInfo.cs:14-15 — "Alphanumeric (X) or alphabetic (A)"), so a class-alphabetic item is admitted, and §15.3 type 2 REQUIRES that — cite.py --check 15.3 "A data item of the class alphabetic or alphanumeric or an alphanumeric literal shall be specified." -> OK (§15.3 rule 2), which also treats a strongly-typed group as alphanumeric and is not excluded by §15.93.3 (unlike §15.59.3/§15.71.3, which state the exclusion). Numeric-edited is admitted as class alphanumeric per §8.5.2.1 Table 2 (the NumericEditedDeEditing member, whose 'i'/'n' exclusion is a different question). POSITIVE side pinned by pb58_argument_predicates_legal line 73 (FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL("12.5") binds) and by the ten literal calls in conformance:cases/15.90.4-Returned-value-rule/intrinsics_test_validators. EDITIONS: batch default — the rule text carries no edition delta, and neither the §15.93 clause nor Annex E/A.4 carries an in-spec attribution for TEST-NUMVAL's introduction edition (grep of specs/ISO_COBOL.md: the only Annex hit is A.4.9 item 12, which is TEST-NUMVAL-C's LOCALE keyword). The compiler's own 2002 window is IntrinsicCatalog's row, which adjudication rule 4 forbids me from using as the derivation.

REFUTED: (verdict SUSTAINED; the missing spec basis supplied and one screening claim independently re-derived): (1) The §15.3-type-2 justification for admitting a class-ALPHABETIC item was the weakest link in this row — §15.93.3 r1 names only "class alphanumeric or national", and the standard demonstrably says "alphabetic" when it means it (§15.96.3 r1 names class alphabetic explicitly), so the omission looked deliberate and the screen looked over-wide. It is not, and the decisive text is one the adjudicator never cited: Table 21, Table of functions (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 29998) gives TEST-NUMVAL's Arguments column as "Anum1 or Nat1", i.e. §15.3 argument TYPE 2 or TYPE 9, and the table's own legend (line 29885 NOTE) fixes that notation. Type 2 admits class alphabetic; type 9 admits "a national group item, a national literal, or an elementary data item of class national". Admissible('s') = [Alphanumeric, NumericEditedDeEditing, National] is exactly type 2 ∪ type 9 under this model, so the union screen coincides with THIS function's rule and there is no over-acceptance to report. (2) I re-derived the rejection claims from the classifier rather than from the negative fixture: an INDEX item is CobolClass.Index by the USAGE-keyed arm of ClassOfPlace (IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs:386), which rides BEFORE the category table — the adjudicator asserted index rejection but the fail-open at Violation() line 910 (candidates.Length == 0 => return null) would have admitted it had that arm not existed. A national GROUP item resolves through Item.AsIfPic.Category => CobolClass.National (line 375-380), so type 9's group form is admitted. (3) Standing test gap, recorded, not verdict-changing (rule 3: CONFORMS with a thin test-ref is legitimate): the rule's NATIONAL alternative is exercised in NEITHER direction — no fixture binds a national literal or national item to TEST-NUMVAL — and the LITERAL half's negative (a numeric literal argument) has no fixture either, though BoundNumericLiteral => CobolClass.Numeric (ClassOf1 line 348) makes it a compile-time COBOL####-class rejection mechanically, not the wrong-stage loud runtime value the Str() default would give. Row stays test-needed. || editions corrected from '85,2002,2014,2023' to 2002,2014,2023 (kb/Work PB3173, S0b; DESIGN-conformance-suite.md §6 step 0): the TEST-NUMVAL function exists from 2002 (IntrinsicCatalog.cs, the COBOL1502 edition window).
